paper_id: Breaking the Hourglass Phenomenon of Residual Quantization_ Enhancing the Upper Bound of Generative Retrieval__oa_W4404783962
title: Breaking the Hourglass Phenomenon of Residual Quantization: Enhancing the Upper Bound of Generative Retrieval
motivation: RQ-based semantic IDs suffer hourglass phenomenon: intermediate tokens overly concentrated, hindering full utilization of generative retrieval in e-commerce.
problem_framing: Define as path sparsity and long-tailed distribution in intermediate codebook layers causing representational capacity bottleneck for GR.
key_insight: Root cause lies in progressive quantization of high-dimensional residuals, naturally producing non-uniform then uniform layer distributions.
method_signature: Two-layer removal: heuristic (drop layer 2 entirely) vs adaptive variable-length token (remove top@K tokens from layer 2).
evaluation_criteria: Recall@K (K=1,3,5,10,30,50) on large-scale e-commerce platform; invalid ID ratio via beam search.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: While simple and efficient, the method is not optimal and can only alleviate, but not completely resolve, the hourglass phenomenon.
evidence_for_taste: path sparsity and long-tail distributions as the primary causes
while this method is simple and efficient, it is not optimal
the performance upper limit of RQ-based methods largely depends on the generation of SID
significantly enhances model performance by improving codebook utilization
